name: Brantly B-2
summary: An American two-seat piston light helicopter from the 1950s; small bubble canopy and a vertically mounted engine behind the cabin.

wings: Three-blade articulated main rotor with narrow blades
engines: Piston engine mounted vertically behind the cabin
Engine bay is small, with louvers or fan cooling
fuselage: Small two-seat bubble canopy with a rounded nose
Skids, wheels or floats; some have a ground-handling wheel
tail: Two-blade tail rotor with a vertical fin and small horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Tiny two-seat bubble helicopter with three narrow rotor blades
Rounded nose and slim boom, sometimes on wheels
Vertical piston engine tucked behind the seats

confusedWith.howToTell: The R22 has a two-blade teetering rotor on a tall thin mast; the Brantly has three narrow blades.
The Enstrom 280 has three seats and a bigger bubble canopy with thick blades; the Brantly is a smaller two-seater.
The Bell 47 has a two-blade rotor and a stabilizer bar and open truss boom; the Brantly has three blades and an enclosed boom.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
